title: Connecting Climate Minds Hub
description: Catalysing a global research community at the intersection of climate change and mental health
content:
We respect your digital privacy. That's why we strictly limit our use of cookies to those that are essential for the smooth functioning of our platform and do not collect private data. For more detailed information, please visit our privacy policy.
Catalysing climate change and mental health research
Explore our rich repository of research agendas, reports, case studies and tools, all designed to support collaboration between disciplines and sectors and accelerate and align the growing field of climate change and mental health research.
Research & Action Agendas
The Connecting Climate Minds Research and Action Agendas set out research priorities to understand and address the needs of people experiencing and responding to the mental health burden of the climate crisis, and priorities to enable this research and translate evidence into action in policy and practice. These agendas aim to support those who are already responding to climate-related mental health challenges by building a more connected and collaborative climate change and mental health field. They also aim to empower people with various forms of expertise across disciplines and sectors to join and make progress in this area by identifying clear priorities and fostering a more inclusive and transdisciplinary field.
Global Agenda
The Global Agenda sets out priorities for climate change and mental health research and action that have been developed from dialogues and consultation with 960+ experts in research, policy, practice, and lived experience in 90 countries.
View Global Agenda
Regional Agendas
The Regional Agendas set out aligned and inclusive priorities for research and action in seven global regions (in line with the Sustainable Development Goal regional groupings), grounded in the needs of those experiencing and responding to climate-related mental health impacts.
View Regional Agendas
Youth Agenda
This agenda sets out priorities for research that can support youth mental health in the context of climate change, and priority actions to enact and translate that research, informed by insights shared by young people around the world.
Summary Agenda
Full Agenda
Youth Declaration
Indigenous Nations and Peoples Agenda
This agenda sets out priorities for research that can inform action to meet the needs of Indigenous People experiencing and responding to the mental health impacts of climate change, informed by insights shared by Indigenous People and communities around the world.
Summary Agenda
Full Agenda
Small Farmer and Fisher Peoples Agenda
This agenda sets out priorities for research that can inform action to meet the needs of small farmers and fisher people experiencing and responding to the mental health impacts of climate change, informed by insights shared by small farmers and fisher people around the world.
Summary Agenda
Full Agenda
How were the agendas developed?
We convened experts across disciplines, sectors and countries in over 20 virtual and in person dialogues. Our impact reports demonstrate and celebrate the diversity of activities and collaboration fostered through Connecting Climate Minds that informed the agendas.
Innovative case studies across the world
Explore our collection of case studies that celebrate the progress being made on the ground to respond to the mental health impacts of climate change.
View Case Studies
Community created toolkits
Our toolkits offer comprehensive guidance on conducting and translating climate change and mental health research. Each toolkit has been carefully crafted by a diverse team to provide practical advice, strategies, and resources, helping you to navigate these complex fields with greater clarity and effectiveness.
Climate Change and Mental Health: An Introductory Toolkit for Researchers
Progress to protect the mental health of increasing numbers of people exposed to climate hazards and to enable climate action that brings co-benefits for mental health depends on researchers from diverse backgrounds bringing their perspectives, methods, and datasets. This toolkit aims to provide researchers from various disciplines with an understanding of why the climate and mental health nexus is important and where research and action are needed for the climate and mental health field based on key emerging insights from Connecting Climate Minds.
View Toolkit
Toolkit for decision-makers taking action to support mental health in the climate crisis
This toolkit aims to provide policymakers, decision-makers, NGOs, and practitioners with a concise overview of the climate-mental health nexus, its importance, key messages, and practical ways to engage.
View Toolkit
Deepening Research & Practice: A Lived Experience Engagement Toolkit by Connecting Climate Minds
Drawing upon the collective wisdom of experts and individuals with firsthand experience and lessons from international collaborations, the toolkit offers practical guidance on navigating the complexities of lived experience engagement in the context of climate change and mental health research and practice.
View Toolkit
How can you get involved?
By joining the Connecting Climate Minds initiative, you will become a part of a growing, global and connected community, who are dedicated to creating a healthier future for both our mental well-being and the planet.
Create an Account
